current.text: He is a locked-in starter for Houston. Tari Eason has not passed him on the depth chart, and Lloyd's projected starting five is VanVleet, Thompson, Durant, Smith and Sengun.
His minutes are stable and higher than Sengun's. Coach Ime Udoka plays his starters very heavy minutes.
With Steven Adams back, he plays more power forward than center.
He is not a high-usage player.
Lloyd sees no reason to expect more blocks, more steals or higher usage this season.
Drafting him around rank 96 is reasonable, but a pick around ESPN's 122 is a better price. Josh believes he can deliver as a late pick.
With a March 28 end date, Houston has a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule, 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He is a 3-and-D role player who is around average in many areas. Smaller, quick guards can beat him on the perimeter.
He will never be a star.
His interior defense, rim deterrence and weak-side shot blocking have grown a lot.
He shot only about 35% on open and wide-open threes, below league average.
He needs to become a more reliable shooter.
His FG% is weak for a forward or center, while he makes many threes for his position.
Josh and Lloyd both call him a boring fantasy pick.

note: He is a cheap, steady starter. Yahoo ranks him 98 at 4 USD, ESPN ranks him 110 at 2 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season, so he is a fine late-auction pick at 1 to 3 USD, and the experts say not to reach for him inside the top 100. He fits punt FG% builds best, since he gives threes and rebounds from a F/C slot with few turnovers. Early in the season, check whether his minutes grow while Durant plays less and whether his better rim defense brings more blocks. His 10-game playoff schedule is a minus.
